subject: [RFC PATCH v1 3/3] xfs: example of devirtualizing buffered write iomap callbacks

reviews.author: Fengnan
reviews.summary: Fengnan reported that enabling iomap_next mode improves performance by 1.6% when used alone, but the gain drops to some extent after enabling it in combination with simple read; they are still investigating potential issues in their modification of iomap_dio_rw.
reviews.raw_body:
First, a brief update on my progress: I modified |iomap_dio_rw| so that 
the XFS direct

I/O read path can support |iomap_next| mode, and ran 4K random read 
performance tests.

Using the performance with both |iomap_next| and simple read disabled as 
the baseline,

enabling only |iomap_next| improved performance by 1.6%; enabling only 
simple read

improved performance by 7.3%; enabling both |iomap_next| and simple read

improved performance by 8.8%.

In non-|iomap_next| mode, |simple read| improves performance by about 10%.
After enabling |iomap_next|, the gain drops somewhat. The changes needed 
to make
|iomap_dio_rw| support |iomap_next| are relatively large, so there may 
be issues in my
current modification. I am still investigating why.

2026-06-29.patch_summary: This patch is an example of devirtualizing buffered write iomap callbacks in the XFS file system. It removes indirect calls by inlining callback functions and allows the compiler to make direct calls, reducing overhead. The patch modifies several files, including iomap/buffered-io.c, iomap/iter.c, xfs/xfs_file.c, and others, adding new functions and modifying existing ones to use the devirtualized callbacks. The goal is to improve performance by eliminating indirect function calls.
